title: Fresh redundancies at Future as tech brands hurt by AI Overviews
key_facts: Future, a UK-based magazine and specialist publisher, is cutting jobs for the second time this year, blaming declines in search traffic; one tech brand's UK audience is down 55% compared with before Google's AI Overviews launched.
Android Central, Tom's Guide and Techradar are among the brands where staff in the UK, US and Canada were told of redundancies in the past week.
Chief executive Kevin Li Ying told staff in a memo seen by Press Gazette that the changes were 'primarily driven by the decline in search'.
The Verge reported that all Android Central staff, including its editor-in-chief and managing editor, were laid off; Future denied the site was closing and said it will continue to publish it.
In January Future made 45 editorial redundancies in its tech divisions, mainly at Techradar and Tom's Guide.
Ipsos iris data: Techradar's UK monthly audience fell from 3.4 million to 2.5 million between January and August (a quarter) and Tom's Guide's from 2.2 million to 1.4 million (38%).
Compared with July 2024, a month before AI Overviews launched in the UK, Techradar is down 35% and Tom's Guide 55%.

Future told investors it expects about 707 million pounds of revenue in the year to 30 September (down 4%), paused its share buyback, and said 15% of group revenue comes from brands that rely mostly on Google; its market value is about 263 million pounds, roughly a tenth of its peak five years ago. The number of roles at risk is unclear.
quote_evidence: UK-based magazine and specialist publishing giant Future is cutting jobs for the second time this year, blaming declines in search traffic as one tech brand’s audience is down 55% in the UK compared to before the launch of Google’s AI Overviews.
Compared to July 2024, a month before AI Overviews officially launched at the top of Google search results in the UK, these brands are down by 35% and 55% respectively.
Future denied that the site was closing altogether and a spokesperson said: “Future will continue to publish Android Central.
why_it_matters_hint: A publisher links job cuts at well-known tech sites to falling search traffic, a sign of how AI answers in search are hitting web publishers.
event_date: Redundancies notified in the week before 5 Oct 2026 (The Verge reported the Android Central layoffs on 1 Oct 2026); Press Gazette article 5 Oct 2026.
notes: Read in full. The memo was seen by Press Gazette; the AI Overviews link is Press Gazette's reading of the audience data, since the memo cites the decline in search generally. The Verge's 1 Oct stories on Android Central (Google News headlines only, not read) mean the underlying event predates 5 Oct; Press Gazette adds the memo, the audience figures and Future's financial notes.
